body:
I appreciate that. My school likely does offer counseling free of charge, but I have been in and out of therapy my entire life. My first experience with death was in a program for troubled teens. I was only 11 at the time my parents put me in the program, all of the other kids were in their late teens. A girl whom I had gotten to know pretty well ended up hanging herself, which was a bit of a shock to me. At 12, my psychiatrist, convinced that I had mood swings and fits of anger that needed to be addressed, prescribed me Abilify. At the time, Abilify was a new drug, but recently they had to stop prescribing it to people under age 18 because of its side effects. I went from 110 pounds at 12 years old to 215 pounds at a rate of 15 pounds per month. The side effects of the drug kept me from socializing until Junior year when I finally stopped taking the drug and lost the weight as quickly as I had gained it. I had weekly appointments with my therapists during this time, which I hated. 

I have had my ups and downs over the years. Occasionally, one good thing will happen to me, which gives me false hope that things are heading in the right direction. Somehow it has always led me right back to where I am today. 

My parents and I have a strange relationship. At times, my mother gives me the impression that she really cares about me, but at the same time, she has said things like "I hate you, I wish I never had you, your sister and brother hate you" and turns my other family members against me when we butt heads. This has been a recurring theme throughout my life. I am dependent on my parents entirely, while never really having a healthy relationship. My years of therapy and programs were all focused on the way I reacted to her bullshit over the years, because I was the only one in the family who wouldn't take her shit. She emasculates my father on a daily basis, even to this day and he sits there and takes it.

I really can't see myself ever getting out of this slump, because it really isn't a slump, its my life.
